segment.description: The upper (headwater) reach of Roan Creek in Johnson County, cold water near the Virginia line in the Roan Mountain drainage, TWRA-stocked as 'Upper Roan Creek'.
segment.boundaries: Catalog covers the upper creek; TWRA's stocking workbook rows are likewise labeled 'Upper Roan Creek' (Johnson County) without mile limits. REACH NOTE: the special trout regulation TWRA sets on Roan Creek - 'Mountain Lake Estates Bridge downstream to Doe Creek' (eregulations Region 4, 2026 live) - applies to the LOWER main stem, a different reach; it is not evidence for the upper creek.

coldSource.notes: Free-flowing mountain headwater creek (catalog: 'Cold Johnson County water near the Virginia line'); no dam or spring source claimed. Nearest gauge evidence is downstream: USGS-03482000 'ROAN CREEK NEAR NEVA, TN' (102 sq mi, below the headwater forks) grabbed 17.0 C on 1988-07-06, while the lower main stem at USGS-03482100 near Doeville (110 sq mi) ran 17.8-26.1 C in summer 1975-76 grabs - a headwater-to-valley warming gradient. No station exists on the stocked upper reach itself. TDEC station records carry '303D' tags on Roan Creek main-stem names (e.g. TDECWPC-ROAN011.6JO); the impairment cause was not verified in this pass. Station identities verified via WQP Station metadata (USGS identity endpoint down this week).

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. TWRA's 2026 stocking program for the water is weekly seasonal stockings (see troutSpecies) with no summer/winter continuity and no posted post-stocking persistence data.

wildPopulation.detail: Brook-trout wild candidacy is NOT borne out by the current official lists: Roan Creek (any reach) appears nowhere on the wild-trout-streams list on TWRA's regulations publisher page (wild list members in this corner of the state are Beaverdam Creek (Johnson Co), Laurel Fork and Left Prong Hampton Creek (Carter Co), Paint Creek and Rocky Fork (Greene/Unicoi), plus Monroe County waters). Another Johnson County wild water (Beaverdam Creek) is on the list, but that fact does not transfer to Roan Creek. No STMP or Cherokee NF document found in this pass documenting a wild trout population in the upper creek.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The nearest gauge below the headwater forks grabbed 17.0 C in July 1988 in a Roan Mountain drainage where the upper reach lies above the valley warming (lower main stem hit 26.1 C), but stocking is spring-to-early-summer only and nothing documents trout persisting year-round.
